newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends higher after intervention.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends higher after intervention.

text.p: The won closed higher against the dollar on Wednesday after the central bank's dollar sales hit the brakes on the local unit's recent falls, dealers said.
The won closed at 869.50 after ranging between 869.10 and 870.10. It opened at 869.90.
"The Bank of Korea's intervention successfully limited the won's slide," said a domestic bank dealer.
The central bank was seen selling dollars in mid-morning trading when the won hit 870.00. "Trading is likely to hover at the current level for the time being," the dealer said.
The central bank declined intervening in the interbank market, as it routinely does.
The won's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 869.90 on Thursday, compared with 868.60 today.
The dollar's rise against the Japanese yen in world markets and the nation's widening trade deficit were main factors for the weak won, dealers said.
The increasing need for overseas financing by some banks after the Hanbo failure added to the won's weakness, they said.
